belief_statement: Preliminary evidence indicates that cool hot season has inconsistent effects on thermal. The evidence base (16 findings, 2 studies) is growing but not yet conclusive.

latent_variables.name: Individual sensitivity differences
latent_variables.rationale: High heterogeneity (high) across findings suggests an unmeasured individual-difference variable moderates the effect of cool hot season on thermal.
latent_variables.suggested_measure: Pre-screening for trait sensitivity or prior exposure

latent_variables.name: Cultural background
latent_variables.rationale: Individual/cultural differences theory is implicated. Cultural norms around nature, noise, or space may moderate effects.

latent_variables.name: Mechanism selection
latent_variables.rationale: Multiple mechanisms are implicated (Psychophysics / Perception, Individual/Cultural Differences, Design Principles). A latent variable may determine which pathway is activated.

latent_variables.name: Dose and duration
latent_variables.rationale: Most studies measure presence/absence of cool hot season, not dose-response curves. Duration and intensity likely matter.
latent_variables.suggested_measure: Parametric variation of intensity and exposure duration

research_needs.question: Does the effect of cool hot season on thermal replicate in a pre-registered RCT?
research_needs.rationale: Current confidence is moderate. A well-powered pre-registered replication would most efficiently resolve the status of this belief.

research_needs.question: What moderates the effect of cool hot season on thermal?
research_needs.rationale: High heterogeneity suggests an unmeasured moderator.

research_needs.question: Which mechanism best explains cool hot season → thermal?
research_needs.rationale: 3 candidate mechanisms exist. Process tracing would identify the active pathway.

research_needs.question: What is the dose-response curve for cool hot season effects on thermal?
research_needs.rationale: Dose-response data enables design guidelines with specific thresholds.
